subject: Fit multiple datasets on the same model (with Laplace approximation) without rebuilding and compiling the model object

messages.author: 5aff2facb9732187
messages.subject: Fit multiple datasets on the same model (with Laplace approximation) without rebuilding and compiling the model object
parts:
Hello!

I am looking to fit a specific model on a large number of simulated datasets. To ensure fast fitting on each dataset, I am using a Laplace approximation. However, I have not found a way to update the data and refit the model without having to rebuild the Laplace object using the `buildLaplace()` function and recompiling it each time. Is there a way to update the data and fit the model without this step?  

See the example below.

Thanks for you help!

Hassen

```
library("nimble")

n     <- 1000
beta  <- 0.2
sigma <- 0.5
X  <- rnorm(n)
Y1 <- rnorm(n, beta*X, sigma) # dataset 1

model_code <- nimbleCode({
  # priors
  beta  ~ dnorm(0, sd = 100)
  sigma ~ dhalfflat()

  # likelihood
  for(i in 1:n) {
    Y[i] ~ dnorm(beta*X[i], sd = sigma)
  }
})

model <- nimbleModel(
  model_code,
  data      = list(Y = Y1),
  constants = list(n = n, X = X),
  inits = list(beta = 0, sigma = 1),
  buildDerivs = TRUE
)

Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)


laplace   <- buildLaplace(model, c('beta','sigma'))
Claplace <- compileNimble(laplace, project = model)


MLE1 <- Claplace$findMLE(c(0, 1))
MLE1$par

#++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
## use new data with the same model

beta  <- -0.5
sigma <- 0.9
Y2    <- rnorm(n, beta*X, sigma) # dataset 2

Cmodel$Y <- Y2 # updating data 

MLE2 <- Claplace$findMLE(c(0, 1)) #------> this does not work properly on the new data
MLE2$par
```

messages.subject: Re: Fit multiple datasets on the same model (with Laplace approximation) without rebuilding and compiling the model object
parts:
Hi Hassen,

This is a good question, but it seems (not sure I am 100% correct) you will have to rebuild and compile your Laplace algorithm (exact MLE in your toy example) again after setting new data in your compiled model code, but without needing to build and compile your model. 

Best wishes,
Wei
